headline: High: Semantic Kernel’s broad network/MCP/file access can amplify Dagster outputs into unsafe actions, while Dagster itself is read-only and non-networked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, MCP, shell, or filesystem write surfaces, so it cannot directly inject Semantic Kernel. The only plausible bridge is manual or application-defined file content into Semantic Kernel, which can parse plugin/tool inputs. That makes the pathway possible but narrow and not default for Dagster.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel ingests Dagster-produced file content as instructions or tool arguments
IF an operator manually copies Dagster output into a Semantic Kernel prompt or plugin input
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between the systems
Restrict Semantic Kernel prompts to structured templates
Add provenance tags to Dagster outputs
Use a read-only handoff file format
requires-engineering: add content filtering before Semantic Kernel tool calls

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no network egress, but Semantic Kernel reads files, uses MCP/APIs, and handles plugin credentials. If Dagster writes artifacts into a shared workspace, Semantic Kernel can ingest them and transmit context to third-party model providers. The leakage path exists in default Semantic Kernel deployments, though Dagster itself is not a direct exfiltrator.
conditions: IF Dagster outputs are placed in a workspace readable by Semantic Kernel
IF Semantic Kernel is configured to call external model providers or MCP/OpenAPI tools
mitigations: Keep Dagster and Semantic Kernel on separate workspaces
Store only redacted artifacts in shared paths
Disable external tool calls for sensitive runs
Rotate plugin credentials before shared execution
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files, modify git, or use network egress, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with Semantic Kernel. Semantic Kernel can write files and use MCP, but without Dagster write access there is no meaningful overlapping write conflict. The pair is therefore mostly read-only from Dagster’s side.
conditions: IF Dagster is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants it write access not shown in the profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable application-defined files
mitigations: Keep Dagster read-only
Separate mutable working directories
Avoid shared git worktrees
Serialize writes through one owner
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster can produce pipeline outputs that Semantic Kernel may treat as application context, and Semantic Kernel’s plugin/tool pattern can act on that context. Because Semantic Kernel is not documented here as verifying Dagster outputs, a bad Dagster result can cascade into downstream actions. Dagster’s lack of execution authority lowers blast radius, but not enough to make this low.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes Dagster outputs without validation
IF Semantic Kernel uses those outputs to call plugins or external APIs
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require schema checks on Dagster outputs
Mark Dagster outputs as untrusted by default
Log and review tool-triggering fields
requires-engineering: add policy gates before plugin execution

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster is open-source and shows no touched data classes or residency constraints, while Semantic Kernel is a Microsoft library that can route data to Azure/OpenAI/Hugging Face and handle plugin credentials. No explicit residency mismatch is documented in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to configuration gaps rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed through Semantic Kernel to non-approved providers
IF the deployment lacks a DPA or residency controls for the chosen model provider
mitigations: Use approved regional model endpoints
Block regulated data in prompts
Document provider DPAs before rollout
Minimize logged prompt content
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
